subject: Competitive eval: model quality comparisons and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@atlasai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive eval follow-up + next steps

Tom — great to chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

1) Goal: run a focused model-quality comparison between Redwood's hosted inference variants and the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex) to validate hallucination rates, factuality, and regression vs your current production baseline.

2) Proposed tests (initial scope):
   - 500 prompt eval set (mix: 150 commonsense/QA, 150 domain knowledge, 200 hallucination probes) — attached as eval-prompt-set.csv.
   - Regression checks: run against your current prod model snapshot to look for drop in exact-match and increase in hallucination on a canonical subset (200 prompts).
   - Metrics: exact match / F1 where applicable, factuality score, hallucination rate (false assertions per 1k tokens), avg latency (p95), and cost per 1k tokens.
   - Blind A/B: if possible, we can run blind human eval for a sampled subset (50-100 items).

3) Logistics:
   - Redwood can run the comparison from our side if you can either share the prompt set + expected golden outputs or grant read-only access to a test dataset.
   - We can also provide a temporary test API key if you prefer to run tests on your side and share results.

4) Timeline: initial run and summary in ~7 business days after we have the dataset or access.

Attached: eval-prompt-set.csv (prompt samples). Also adding links to a quick test-config.yaml stub and SOC2 evidence request we use for customers.

Can you confirm the dataset delivery option (share vs grant access), and who from procurement we should loop in for the test account & NDAs?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate infra with Aditya and Neha once we get confirmation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

--
Attachment: eval-prompt-set.csv (csv, 18KB)

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@atlasai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah@atlasai.com>, procurement@atlasai.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up + next steps

Thanks, Marissa — really helpful summary. We want to move forward with a Redwood-run comparison if you can. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- We'll share the prompt set and golden answers for the QA items; for hallucination probes we can provide reference sources for adjudication.
- Metrics to prioritize: exact match (where applicable), Factuality score (binary adjudication per response), hallucination rate (false assertions per 100 responses), and latency (p95). Cost per 1k tokens is useful but secondary for this stage.
- Can you include the hyperscaler variants you plan to test (specific model names) and whether Redwood will test quantized variants?

Procurement FYI: procurement@atlasai.com — they’ll take care of temporary test-account paperwork / NDAs.

Two asks:
1) Can you provide temporary test API keys or a secure test endpoint so we can run a few smoke tests ourselves?
2) Do you have a brief doc on your data handling for test payloads (we prefer not to send PII; will scrub before sharing)?

If helpful, we can set a quick 20-min call tomorrow to confirm datasets and timelines.

—Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of ML Platforms | Atlas AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@atlasai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up + next steps

Thanks Tom — copied procurement and looping in our infra/ML leads so we can scope the runs. Quick answers and an outline for the test plan: 

Hyperscaler model list (we’ll include exact model strings in the test-config):
 - AWS Bedrock: claude-instant-v1 / bedrock-gemini-2-lite (depending on availability)
 - GCP Vertex: text-bison / vertex-gemini-small
 - Redwood variants: redwood-verified-base (float16) and redwood-quant-4bit (latency-optimized)

Quantization: yes — we’ll include a quantized 4-bit variant for Redwood where applicable. Hyperscalers will be run at the public/default precision available on their endpoints (we’ll note settings).

Planned evaluation workflow:
1) Run the 500-prompt evaluation across all variants (exact-match / token-level metrics where applicable).
2) Run the 200-prompt regression subset against your provided golden answers to flag any quality regressions.
3) Run hallucination probes and collect factuality adjudications (we’ll surface candidate hallucinations for your SMEs to adjudicate).
4) Collect latency & cost metrics with identical payloads and upstream routing (note: exact cost comparisons are approximate due to different billing models).
5) Produce a concise report with charts, example failure cases, and recommended configuration (batching, quantization) for production parity.

We can provide temporary read-only API keys for Redwood-hosted test endpoints and a secure S3 Share for you to drop the prompt/golden files. I’ll have Aditya coordinate the keys & S3 link once procurement confirms.

Doc attached: test-config.yaml (stub) and SOC2-request.pdf — the latter answers the basic data handling Qs you raised. We handle test payloads in isolated test projects with logs retained for 30 days by default; sensitive data should be scrubbed before upload — happy to run on-prem/private deploys for sensitive workloads if needed.

Timeline: we’ll aim to deliver an initial comparison dashboard in 7 business days after we have the data and the test-access agreement. Can procurement loop in an NDA/test-account contact and preferred S3 bucket?

Next steps:
 - procurement@atlasai.com to confirm NDA/test-account
 - Atlas to share prompt set + golden answers (S3 link or upload)
 - Redwood to provision test keys & schedule runs (Aditya/Neha/Rishi to coordinate)

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachments: test-config.yaml (yaml, 3KB), SOC2-request.pdf (pdf, 125KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Atlas eval infra & capacity

Internal note — quick infra checklist for the Atlas run (deal RWF-2026-ATL-1532):

- Need to provision a temporary dedicated test pool (2x A100-equivalent vGPU) for consistent latency runs across 48 hours.
- Allocate a test API key with RBAC limiting (no access to customer data beyond this test). TTL: 14 days.
- Test-config.yaml: include model strings (Marissa — add exact hyperscaler strings once confirmed).
- Adjudication: we should prepare a simple UI for Atlas SMEs to label hallucinations (binary + comment). Could reuse our internal eval portal; need an account for Tom/Sarah.

I’ll start a runbook and milestone timeline: smoke tests day 0, full run days 1-2, report draft day 5. If procurement stalls, we can still run a Redwood-only comparison with public prompts to show the methodology.

Neha
Neha Kapoor | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
